'''Cochinita pibil''' (also '''puerco pibil''') is a traditional [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Mexico|Mexican]] slow-roasted (braised) pork dish from the Yucatán.

This version of the dish was adapted from [[Wikipedia:Robert Rodríguez|Robert Rodríguez]]'s DVD extras on ''[[Wikipedia:Once Upon a Time in Mexico|Once Upon a Time in Mexico]]''.  

==Ingredients==

* 5 [[Cookbook:tablespoon|Tbsp]] (75 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]]) [[cookbook:annatto|annatto]] seeds
* 2 [[Cookbook:teaspoon|tsp]] (10 ml) [[Cookbook:cumin|cumin]] seeds
* 1 Tbsp (15 ml) [[Cookbook:Pepper|peppercorns]]
* 8 [[Cookbook:allspice|allspice]] berries
* ½ tsp (8 ml) whole [[Cookbook:clove|cloves]]
* 2 [[Cookbook:chile peppers|habanero chile]]s (or milder chiles)
* ½ [[Cookbook:cup|cup]] (120 ml) [[Cookbook:orange |orange]] juice
* ½ cup (120 ml) white [[Cookbook:vinegar|vinegar]]
* 2 Tbsp (30 ml) [[Cookbook:salt|salt]]
* 8 cloves of [[Cookbook:garlic|garlic]]
* 5 [[Cookbook:lemon|lemon]]s, juiced
* 1 splash of [[Bartending/Alcohol/Spirits#Tequila|tequila]]
* 5 [[Cookbook:Pound|pounds]] (2.3 [[Cookbook:Kilogram|kg]]) [[Cookbook:pork|pork]] butt
* [[Cookbook:Banana|Banana]] leaves and/or heavy-duty [[Cookbook:Aluminium Foil|aluminium foil]]
* White or Spanish [[Cookbook:rice|rice]], [[Cookbook:taco|taco]] shells, or [[Cookbook:tortilla|tortilla]]s for serving

== Procedure ==

# Place the annatto, cumin, peppercorns, allspice, and cloves in a spice grinder and process to a fine powder. You can use an electric coffee grinder for the spices, but it will not be suitable for coffee afterwards.
# Remove the seeds and veins from the habanero chiles and chop coarsely. If you want a hotter dish, leave some of the veins and seeds in.
# Process the orange juice, vinegar, chiles, salt, garlic, and the spice powder in a [[Cookbook:blender|blender]] or [[Cookbook:food processor|food processor]] until liquefied. Add the lemon juice and tequila.
# Cut the pork into 2-inch (5 cm) chunks. Leave the fat on the meat, to keep the pork moist while roasting; you can remove it after cooking if you wish.
# Place pork in a large, self-sealing plastic bag with the [[Cookbook:marinade|marinade]]. Seal bag and turn to evenly coat the meat. Refrigerate for 8 to 24 hours, turning occasionally.
# Heat [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] to 325°F (160°C). Dump the meat and the marinade in a roasting pan lined with banana leaves or foil, making sure to wrap tightly so no steam escapes.  If using banana leaves, an outer wrapping with foil will help seal in the steam.
# Bake for 4 hours. Open packet carefully; the meat should shred easily with a fork.
# Serve over rice, or shred and serve with taco shells or tortillas. 

==Nutrition==

Per serving: 240 calories (84 fat calories), 9.3 g fat (2.9 g saturated, 3.8 g monounsaturated), 92.2 mg cholesterol, 33.1 g protein, 5.2 g carbohydrates, 0.7 g fiber, 1037 mg sodium.
